title: Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level
main_claim: Setting: split semisimple G over a global function field, at any full finite level D. The rational and Q̄_ℓ cusp spaces split as a direct sum over the nilpotent orbits of the dual group. Each summand has its Satake parameters in r_O·(compact part of the JM centralizer) at every good place and every complex embedding. This proves GLR Conjectures 3.4.5 and 3.4.6 when D=0. A corollary: for adjoint absolutely simple G, a cuspidal π that is generic at one unramified place is tempered at every unramified place.

issues.description: The final step depends entirely on Ciubotaru-Harris Corollary 6.32(1): a generic, unitary, spherical representation with a geometric (half-integral) Satake parameter has polar exponent zero. I could not check that citation's exact hypotheses (for example any restriction on q or the characteristic) against this setting. This is a reliance on an outside result, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: By [CiubotaruHarris, Corollary 6.32(1)], its polar exponent is zero. Hence mu_O=0.

issues.description: Not checked in detail. The amplitude bound and the extreme transfer depend on several Section 2 results: Prop cat:loops (the spherical trace as a module over the Koszul algebra of Ad(s)e=q^d e), Theorem cat:central (Wakimoto filtration with interchange and Weil compatibility), Prop cat:hecke (identifying e_v H^ with spherical cohomology) and Prop cat:cyclic (Frobenius equals T_u on M(u)). I read the statements as they are used downstream and found them internally consistent, but did not verify the proofs. No gap is claimed.
issues.evidence: The cohomology transfer in Proposition cat:hecke identifies e_v H^_mu with H^*(C^sph_{mu,v}) tensor R_x and intertwines S_x and the center.

coverage: Read in full: introduction, Section 4 (rotation trace identity: boundedness/genericity, the finite correspondence for a translation, large-Frobenius trace via rigidification, the apartment/strong-regularity argument, Lemma rot:anisotropic, the Picard/Lang descent comparison and its multidegree-zero argument), Section 5 and Section 6. Section 5 covers the Hecke ideal detector Lemma ext:hecke and its convention check (dominant means 1-Qr(α^∨)≠0, consistent with the trivial representation being a Langlands quotient), the spectral facts, the spectral-gap lemma with its induction on rank, Prop ext:lower (trace asymptotics: discrete part dim·P·a^n against continuous part rank(Q_n)·Cr^n plus the discrete tail), rationality, unique extreme weight, extreme transfer, the spherical chain projector, the Koszul top-degree lemma and the final contradiction. Section 6 covers alignment of the embeddings with the (δ,δ)=0 argument, orbit uniqueness via [g_0,e]=g_2, Galois sign corrections, twist-purity from L. Lafforgue, place independence, rational descent by idempotents, and the generic corollary. Section 3: read Prop amp:geometry, the tests, specialization, Levi tests, resonance orbits, orbit contributions, bounded corrected fibers (including the open-orbit/boundary-orbit case split) and Theorem amp:amplitude. By hand I checked the squared-gap identity 2⟨λ,μ⟩−⟨μ,h⟩ = 2m‖λ−h/2‖², using (h,λ−h/2)=0 from compatibility, and that it matches the introduction's formula. I also checked the degree bookkeeping: the lower bound 2dm‖λ0‖²+b against the upper bound C+dm·max⟨λ0,h_e⟩. Section 2 (categorical trace, derived Satake, Wakimoto) was only checked as stated where it is used.
